# Results {#sec-results}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Read finished statistics across the boundary (fast read of a saved result;
# this does NOT re-run the analysis).
#
# Anchor on the `.here` sentinel at the research-programme root via rprojroot,
# NOT here::here(): `here` treats this book's _quarto.yml as a project root and
# would stop here instead of walking up to the shared analysis folder.
library(readr)
root  <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file(".here"))
stats <- read_csv(file.path(root, "shared-resources", "derived", "example-stats.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Addressing the aims set out in @sec-aims, the example analysis included
`r stats$n` participants. The estimated treatment–control difference in the
biomarker was
`r sprintf("%.2f (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f; p = %.3f)", stats$estimate, stats$conf_low, stats$conf_high, stats$p_value)`.

![Biomarker by group — the same figure file the journal paper embeds, synced in from `shared-resources/figures/`.](/figures/example-figure.png){#fig-thesis-example width=85%}

@fig-thesis-example shows the distribution.
